newsitem.title: USA: South Asia could eventually speed up - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: South Asia could eventually speed up - World Bank.

text.p: A World Bank official on Friday said that South Asia has a good chance of accelerating its growth by early in the new century if it increased domestic savings and continued on the reform path.
But John Williamson, Bank chief economist for the region, told a briefing for reporters that budget deficits in several countries of the area are still higher than the Bank would like to see.

Overall, he said that the Bank believed that the strong economic growth in the region was not a "flash in the pan and looks set to continue what it has done in recent years and with luck ... has a chance of accelerating to 7 or 8 precent a year."
Williamson met with reporters in conjunction with the semi-annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
He said that while savings rates in the region were respectable, they were probably not high enough to support growth very much larger than about six percent a year in the medium term.

He noted that India has had growth rates of 7 percent or close to it for four years but, "I think it is going to be difficult to maintain that in the longer term... unless there is some further increase in savings."

But he said there was a good chance that a savings increase would occur since decent growth in itself tends to encourage added savings. Moreover, the potential for increased savings is being helped in the region by declining fertility rates.
